item.title: Jersey Mike’s IPO Said to Be More Than 10 Times Oversubscribed
item.description: Jersey Mike’s Subs Inc.’s initial public offering has attracted investor demand for more than 10 times the available shares ahead of pricing on Wednesday, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Southern Africa Payments Hub Eyes More Currencies to Boost Trade
item.description: A multibillion-dollar cross-border payments platform serving southern Africa plans to expand beyond the South African rand and Angolan kwanza, widening the range of currencies it supports to lower transaction costs and boost trade.

item.title: Amazon Seeks FCC Nod to Beam Satellite Coverage to Mobile Phones
item.description: Amazon.com Inc. has requested permission from the US Federal Communications Commission to launch a direct-to-device network of 5,000 satellites to provide mobile services to cell phones from space, furthering the company’s competition with SpaceX.

item.title: Tyson, JBS Shares Surge as US Reopens Mexico Cattle Imports After Screwworm Ban
item.description: Shares of meatpackers Tyson Foods Inc. and JBS NV surged after the US said it would resume cattle shipments from Mexico, easing a domestic shortage that has led to higher costs for their animals.

item.title: Corporate Bonds Lose Appeal as Shock Absorber, Carlyle Says
item.description: As corporate bonds become less reliable at protecting against market shocks, investors are looking to asset-backed finance as an alternative source of stability, according to Carlyle Group.

item.title: ASML Slides on Report of China Starting DUV Tool Production
item.description: ASML Holding NV shares slid to the lowest since early June after a report that a Chinese state-backed company has begun mass producing certain chipmaking machines, posing a potential threat to the Dutch firm’s sales.

item.title: Citi Traders Are Betting Fed Will Keep Rates on Hold This Week
item.description: Citigroup Inc.’s traders are betting the Federal Reserve will leave rates unchanged this week, even as the swap markets assign a more than one-in-three chance of a quarter-point hike.

item.title: Nvidia Credit Risk Jumps in Swaps Market on AI Deal Talk Reports
item.description: The cost of protecting Nvidia Corp.’s debt against default surged by the most on record on Monday after reports that the chipmaker is in conversations on more than $750 billion of artificial intelligence infrastructure deals, stoking fears that the company is taking on even more obligations.

item.title: Robeco’s $18 Billion Stock Picker Bets on Argentina After Hiatus
item.description: It took nearly a decade for one of Europe’s biggest emerging-market investors to return to Argentine stocks.

item.title: Biggest State Street Debate Is Where Bessent Bond Gauge Goes
item.description: The most involved discussion at State Street Corp.’s $6 trillion investment-management arm is around the outlook for 10-year US Treasury yields — the main financial metric targeted by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

item.title: Ares Bundles €3 Billion of Private Credit for Secondaries Sale
item.description: Ares Management Corp. is preparing to sell €3 billion ($3.4 billion) of bundled stakes in a flagship European direct-lending fund, one of the largest credit-secondaries deals ever.

item.title: Nvidia Makes ‘Substantial’ Investment in Sutskever’s Startup
item.description: Nvidia Corp. said it has made a “substantial” investment in Safe Superintelligence Inc., the artificial intelligence startup co-founded by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever.

item.title: Chile Taps International Bond Markets After Debt Limit Raise
item.description: Chile is returning to international debt markets for the second time in 2026, just a few weeks after Congress raised the limit on sovereign bond sales this year.

item.title: SNB Expects to Keep Interest Rate at Zero Until End of 2027
item.description: The Swiss National Bank is set to keep its key interest rate at zero until the end of 2027 before probably starting to raise it, according to people familiar with the thinking inside the central bank.

item.title: Treasury Yields Follow Oil Lower With Fed and Supply in Focus
item.description: US Treasuries edged higher as oil prices softened after the US paused its nearly two-week campaign of strikes against Iran, while traders eyed a roughly one-in-three chance of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike on Wednesday.

item.title: US Core Capital Goods Orders Climb by More Than Expected
item.description: US orders for business equipment rose in June by more than projected, capping robust capital investment across the first half of the year.

item.title: Fintech Plata Adds Ex-Regulator, Former Ambassador to US Board
item.description: Fintech Plata tapped a former US regulator and a former US ambassador to Russia to join the board of its US holding company as the lender expands into Colombia and eyes an eventual public listing.

item.title: Arnault Joins X as LVMH CEO Fights Off Rumors of Family Disunity
item.description: Europe’s richest person has finally joined the social media fray.

item.title: Chile Rates Seen on Hold as War Upends Expectations for Year End
item.description: Chile’s central bank is expected to hold its benchmark interest rate unchanged for a fifth straight meeting on Tuesday, a point of stability in a market whipsawed by events in the Middle East.

item.title: Canadians’ Pessimism About Economy Is Fading Despite Trade War, Poll Says
item.description: Canadians are shaking off months of economic pessimism as worries about weak growth and higher energy prices fade.

item.title: China Says US Pledged to Cap Replacement Tariffs at 20%
item.description: China said the US had committed to cap replacement tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, staking out a limit on further increases after US President Donald Trump imposed a new levy.

item.title: Crisis-Level Swings Become New Normal in 2026 Stock Market
item.description: Forget the VIX at 18. The stock market is swinging around in ways that are beyond what’s seen as normal in bull markets.

item.title: Shipping Upheaval Suggests Oil Selloff Won’t Last
item.description: The US and Iran may be holding fire, but costly cargo diversions are already underway.

item.title: Shionogi-Backed Apnimed Seeks to Raise $160 Million in US IPO
item.description: Apnimed Inc., a late-stage drug developer focused on sleep apnea, is seeking to raise as much as $160 million in a US initial public offering.

item.title: Truist Names Jefferies Veteran Mineard Co-Head of TMT
item.description: Craig Mineard is joining Truist Financial Corp.’s investment bank from Jefferies Financial Group Inc. to co-head the firm’s technology media and telecom group.

item.title: Crypto Treasury Firms Pivot to AI in Bid to Win Back Investors
item.description: The implosion of the once-hot market for cryptocurrency treasury stocks is prompting a number of firms to pivot to artificial intelligence in an attempt to win back investors. So far, it isn’t working.

item.title: US Stocks Catch a Bid as Oil Tumbles With Iran Conflict Pause
item.description: US stock futures rallied as oil prices slid with the US pausing strikes against Iran and tankers sailing for a recently-disrupted Kazakh export terminal, easing supply pressures.

item.title: China Vows Response to US Sanctions Threat Against AI Firms
item.description: China warned it would take “all necessary measures” if the US moves to sanction Chinese artificial intelligence companies over allegations they improperly used American models to train their own systems.

item.title: Samsung Shows Smart Glasses Still Work Best Tied to a Phone
item.description: Today’s products perform best when connected to partner devices

item.title: From US to Japan, Policymakers Aim to Get Capital Moving Where They Want
item.description: Officials are now turning their jawbone tactics on government debt as borrowing costs soar.
